description: Conversation-style evaluation cases for the OpenStudio MCP Model Workspace Agent.

cases.query: Can you inspect examples/openstudio_mcp_demo/resource/sample.osm and give me a concise senior-modeler summary of the building geometry, spaces, thermal zones, surfaces, and subsurfaces?

expected_output.style: concise professional building energy modeler summary

pass_criteria: Does not run simulation.
Uses OpenStudio SDK inspection.
Uses model.getBuildingStorys() if building stories are inspected.
Returns a readable summary plus structured counts or JSON artifact.

cases.query: For the sample model, calculate overall WWR and WWR by north/east/south/west orientation. Please explain how you handled azimuth.

summary_should_include: exterior wall area and window area

pass_criteria: Converts surface.azimuth() from radians to degrees using openstudio.convert.
Does not manually assume azimuth is already degrees.
Reports units and orientation-bin assumptions.

cases.query: Inspect the envelope constructions in sample.osm. I want exterior walls, roofs, floors, windows, doors, and skylights with their construction names and material layers.
pass_criteria: Does not edit the model.
Uses construction optional checks before unwrapping.
Separates opaque and fenestration constructions when practical.

cases.query: For the exterior opaque constructions in the sample model, extract material thickness, conductivity, density, specific heat, and thermal resistance where available.
pass_criteria: Handles missing material methods without crashing.
Does not claim every material has every property.
Reports units for material properties.

cases.query: Review the schedules in the sample model. Focus on occupancy, lighting, electric equipment, thermostat setpoints, and HVAC availability schedules by space type or thermal zone.

summary_should_include: schedule usage by space type or zone
default day values or profile summary

pass_criteria: Does not run simulation.
Uses schedule optional checks.
Explains whether findings are model inputs, not simulated results.

cases.query: Summarize people, lights, electric equipment, gas equipment, and outdoor air loads in sample.osm by space and space type. I want this as a practical load QA report.

summary_should_include: loads by space type where available
load density or total design load

pass_criteria: Separates design/input load inspection from simulation results.
Handles absent gas equipment or outdoor air objects gracefully.
Reports units.

cases.query: Inspect the HVAC topology in the sample model. Tell me what air loops, plant loops, zone equipment, thermostats, coils, fans, and served zones exist.
pass_criteria: Does not invent HVAC systems when none exist.
Reports missing getters or absent objects as warnings.
Does not run simulation.

cases.query: Create a copy of the sample model and reduce all lighting power by 20 percent. Show me exactly what script you will run before executing.

summary_should_include: recommended validation or simulation next step

pass_criteria: Preserves the original input model.
Writes to a copied output model.
Reports before and after values for every changed lighting definition.
Does not execute until explicit approval is obtained.

cases.query: Make a copied model where south-facing WWR is reduced to 20 percent. If you need any assumptions, state them before running.

expected_output.style: careful edit plan and change report

pass_criteria: Clarifies how to handle windows on surfaces near south orientation if ambiguous.
Uses azimuth conversion through openstudio.convert.
Does not overwrite the original model.
Recommends MCP model validation and simulation after edit.

cases.query: Add an F-factor slab construction to the sample model. Use default values if needed.

summary_should_include: clarifying question or explicit default assumptions
candidate assignment targets if assigning to model objects

pass_criteria: Asks for name, F-factor value and units, area value and units, and exposed perimeter value and units.
Explains OpenStudio setters expect SI values.
If user permits defaults, lists assumptions as Object:Name.parameter: assumed to be x.
Does not create the object before clarification or explicit default approval.
